More than a year after #MeToo became a global call to action, how much has changed? 
@Aijenpoo and other girl bosses are digging into this question at the #nytnewrules summit. https://t.co/juql6OHpZu

#MeToo has become a global call to action, transforming the conversation around gender, power and who gets a seat at what table. But how much has really changed?

NDWA’s @aijenpoo joins #nytnewrules tomorrow to discuss. Follow @nytlive for updates!

https://t.co/NC05aFrflg https://t.co/3HxsCiVNrB

Happening today! NDWA Director @aijenpoo will be there to weigh in on the progress of the #MeToo movement and the challenges that lie ahead. Follow @nytlive for updates! 
https://t.co/d4AoQra7s7

Our director @aijenpoo is right! Women have been showing up for each other across industries to make all of our #Metoo stories visible. Only through collective organizing and shared power can we incite policy changes that uplift us all.  
https://t.co/T6eGkkYvCZ
Pay attention! Women are catalyzing the #MeToo moment into a powerful force for real, concrete change at all levels. https://t.co/T6eGkkYvCZ

"There is trafficking happening all around us. Many workers from overseas have little information about the situations they are getting into.” - Judith, trafficking survivor and domestic worker leader. Read her story: https://t.co/5Dd0fPwS00
 #TimesUp #MeToo https://t.co/603OzEMCbU

NDWA leader Adriana spoke out about the pressure to stay quiet after being sexually harassed on the job and why the voices of domestic workers are essential to the #MeToo movement. 
https://t.co/iWKYj3GpJ1

“Many of us have come forward to say #MeToo and joined a movement with other women to say #TimesUp on sexual harassment. And now we’re taking a big step forward around sexual harassment in domestic work, and we’re demanding dignity and respect everywhere.” -June, caregiver https://t.co/9YAb9gs3ZQ
June Barrett's #MeToo story is why we fight for #Dignity4AllWorkers. https://t.co/MaWGG8NbFA

Today marks the 5th anniversary of Mike Brown’s murder at the hands of police. Rise in power Mike. And thank you to the organizers in Ferguson and across the world who showed all of us a path to dignity and freedom. #BlackLivesMatter always and forever. https://t.co/n7NY8vyvU5

Firing Daniel Pantaleo, the officer who murdered #EricGarner, is the smallest step toward justice achieved only by Eric's family's unwavering commitment to accountability and organizers' work to stop racist acts of police brutality. #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/C8RcXB3qCA

Our very own domestic worker leader June took the ✨international stage✨ at the #MeToo Summit in Iceland to talk about how to successfully build collective power among women of color survivors. #metooReykjavik. https://t.co/LUJOIfd31L

“Policy change alone will not end this problem. A culture shift is also needed to prevent the sexual harassment that women of colour, migrants, low-paid workers and others, routinely experience.” - @aijenpoo #MeToo

In the two years since #MeToo broke online, domestic workers have told our stories online, in private, and in the streets. We have supported one another. We have organized. We have pushed for policy change. 

We will not be ignored. 
https://t.co/TR677TzG6J

#MeToo 
#WithYou
#DontTellMeHowToDress
#BabaeAko
All around the world Asian women are defying stereotypes and fighting sexual harassment.

#MeToo: two years since survivors took @taranaburke’s hashtag viral, each new story reminding survivors everywhere that they are not alone. https://t.co/Ub5IPk9KX4

We are here in solidarity with the millions of brave women, from domestic workers to farm workers to women in Hollywood, who courageously share their experiences of sexual assault in the workplace and advocate for change. #MeToo https://t.co/Px5CJbBPxb
Stories like June's are why we continue to fight for protections for ALL workers — and why we need the #BeHEARD Act and National #DomesticWorkersBillofRights. #MeToo https://t.co/QPcvwzET7y

Domestic worker leader Myrla Baldonado found the courage to speak out about sexual harassment. She’s testified on the Hill to urge Congress to pass the #BeHEARD Act and the National #DomesticWorkersBillofRights to make workplaces safer for women. #MeToo https://t.co/MnpB9oMi08

Daniela told her #MeToo story after hearing other brave women share their stories of sexual harassment. She and millions of other domestic workers are urging Congress to pass the National #DomesticWorkersBillofRights and the #BeHeard Act to make all workplaces safer.
Thank you Daniela and all of the domestic worker women who are building a network of support and healing for survivors everywhere. #MeToo https://t.co/bCat6sFNyF

This month, two years after strong, courageous survivors started a global conversation, we’re working with @meetoomvt, @nwlc, @mujerxsrising to take #MeToo to the next level. 

Learn more about #MeTooVoter: https://t.co/MxBiy09ZAW https://t.co/SgoyQeAsKM

The #MeToo movement is more than a conversation -- it’s been a catalyst for action. And we’re bringing that energy to the ballot box with #MeTooVoter 🗳

Watch to learn more: 
https://t.co/DQBDrU5xoO

The #MeToo movement opened the conversation. We need to continue the momentum and enact laws that provide protection for millions of workers who have been left out. The #BEHEARD in the Workplace Act does just that. Learn more at https://t.co/PSW7e4FmYY. https://t.co/NBbkj0O2su

WATCH: Domestic worker leader June Barrett shine on @fullfrontalsamb! She talked about how we’re *aggressively organizing* for a National #DomesticWorkersBillofRights on behalf of everyone who has said #MeToo. https://t.co/Nhhc0I6wmt

If you missed domestic worker leader June Barrett on @fullfrontalsamb, read her #MeToo story to learn why we’re aggressively organizing for a National #DomesticWorkersBillofRights that will protect *all* workers from sexual assault in the workplace. https://t.co/FamYYUCL1n

From #MeToo to #FamiliesBelongTogether, domestic workers are leaders in movements for freedom and justice. That’s why we organize to win #Dignity4AllWorkers.  
https://t.co/669ZXaz2jG

#MeTooVoters won the first question about sexual assault at a presidential debate in 20 years, but that’s not enough. We need candidates to recognize #MeToo voters as a powerful political force and offer solutions to make our country safer. 
https://t.co/jVldY1R1kB

@IDWFED @fams2gether @alfonsocuaron @Participant @ROMACuaron Domestic workers joined with Hollywood A-listers and farmworker women to help to say #MeToo. Together, we built a network of support and healing for survivors everywhere and catalyzed significant policy change at the state and local level. https://t.co/pzOLJJDM44

Sending love to survivors everywhere today. #TimesUp #MeToo

The #MeToo Movement "speaks to the needs of all survivors. It addresses sexual violence as a systemic issue — and it explains how other systemic issues, such as anti-black racism, capitalism and classism, poverty & housing impact survivors." @TaranaBurke 
https://t.co/hSVjWWlWWt

When Michelle Williams invited @TaranaBurke to the 2018 #GoldenGlobes, the two started organizing to bring more activists -- including our own @AijenPoo -- to the red carpet. Their inclusive vision continues to shape the #MeToo movement.
https://t.co/TVX3yk8Qbv

The brave women who told their #MeToo stories inspired thousands of other women to come forward and join the movement to end sexual assault.

Making #BlackLivesMatter in the labor movement: "Building the kinds of movements that Black women need to shape a new economy & a new democracy that don’t force them to choose between making a living and being a part of a healthy democracy.” -@AliciaGarza
https://t.co/ksel8iGzfL
